subject: Request: Processing boundaries and no-model-learning scope for StratusHealth POC
messages:
From: Mike Turner <mike.turner@stratushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@stratushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC: data processing boundaries & DPA amendments

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo last week. We have greenlit a 6-week POC but our legal/compliance team needs clarification on a few items before we can start ingesting any PHI-adjacent test data:

1) No-model-learning: we need an explicit commitment that StratusHealth data will not be used to train or improve Redwood models (including internal model-tuning) for the duration of the POC and for production if we sign a long-term agreement.
2) Subprocessors: full list of subprocessors that will process customer content (hosting, logging, monitoring, telemetry) and their locations.
3) Cross-border transfers: We require that data remain in the US for this POC and an explanation of how data residency is enforced.
4) Evidence: SOC 2 + any recent penetration test summaries and an exportable evidence bundle for procurement.

Can you confirm your position on each item and point me to the DPA clause language you recommend? Procurement will attach a redline if anything is off.

Appreciate a concise answer so I can push internally.

—Mike
Mike Turner
Head of IT Procurement, StratusHealth

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: data processing boundaries & DPA amendments

Mike —

Thanks for the clear checklist. Short answers up front, followed by specifics we can put into a DPA addendum for the POC: 

- No-model-learning: Redwood can commit that customer content will not be used to improve our public or internal models for the POC period and for any production environment tied to a signed agreement where "no model learning" is selected. We will add a no-training addendum (simple opt-out flag) to the DPA that explicitly covers: model training, continual fine-tuning, prompt/response aggregation for model improvement, and human-in-the-loop labeling programs.

- Subprocessors: we will provide a snapshot inventory and are prepared to include a carveout process in the DPA for any future subprocessor additions. For the POC the primary processors are: AWS (us-east-1) for core hosting, Google Cloud (us-west2) for regional failover, and FastEdge GPU services (contracted infra provider) for burst GPU capacity. All telemetry that contains customer content is routed to the same regions and is protected per our encryption and access controls.

- Cross-border transfers: for the POC we can restrict processing to US-only regions and enforce that by provisioning POC tenants in us-east-1 with strict routing. If you need contractual guarantees we can include an EU/US transfer clause if the conversation expands, but for now we will bind the POC to US residency.

- Evidence: we will hand over an evidence bundle (SOC 2 Type II summary, recent pentest executive summary, subprocessors list, and our dataflow diagram). I have asked Laura to prepare the export-ready package and a short technical note describing how we implement the no-training flag at the runtime level (prefix filtering, KV cache isolation).

Next steps: Laura will produce a DPA addendum language draft you can attach to your procurement redline. Can you confirm the exact signatories (legal + procurement) and the deadline for POC kickoff?

Best,
Marcus
VP, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Anna Silva <anna.silva@stratushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Mike Turner <mike.turner@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@stratushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: data processing boundaries & DPA amendments

Marcus / team —

Quick follow-ups from legal counsel: 

1) Derivative rights: our contracts need language clarifying whether outputs (model responses) generated from our prompts are considered StratusHealth IP vs. Redwood output. For a healthcare POC we want a guarantee that any outputs derived from customer-provided content are exportable and that Redwood will not claim rights to derivative datasets.

2) Export controls & regulated data: please confirm any geolocation enforcement and whether any subprocessors might have access from non-US personnel (support, SRE) that could trigger export/regulatory concerns. If Redwood uses contractors or a global SRE team to debug, we need to know controls or a waiver process.

3) Auditability: can Redwood provide an auditable record (log) showing that the no-training flag was active for tenant X during the POC period? We understand that some proof may be operational (config + runtime logs) rather than model weights snapshots.

If you can bake those points into the DPA addendum and provide a draft today or tomorrow that would keep the procurement timeline intact.

Thanks,
Anna Silva
GTM Counsel, StratusHealth

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Anna Silva <anna.silva@stratushealth.com>, Mike Turner <mike.turner@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: data processing boundaries & DPA amendments

Anna / Mike —

Thanks — below are concrete items we'll include in the DPA addendum and the evidence bundle (attached):

- No-training / Derivative rights: DPA addendum will include an explicit "No Model Learning" clause and an outputs ownership paragraph: StratusHealth owns prompts and prompt-derived outputs for the duration of the engagement; Redwood grants a limited runtime license to serve responses but will not use customer content or generated outputs to create derivative training datasets. We will also include a 1-year post-termination deletion window for retained logs unless you request immediate purge.

- Subprocessors & access controls: attached is the current subprocessor inventory (snapshot dated 2026-06-18). Access from non-US personnel is limited: support/SRE access is role-based and requires elevated approval; cross-border access is logged and requires a specific incident/exemption. We will include the approval flow and a point-of-contact for any emergency remote access.

- Export controls / geofencing: technical isolation is enforced by tenant provisioning in us-east-1 and route tables that prevent egress to other regions. Our platform enforces region-locked data paths at the network and orchestration layer for POC tenants. We'll add contractual language that we will not intentionally transfer POC customer content outside the US without prior written consent.

- Auditability: we can provide an auditable evidence bundle that contains: tenant-level config snapshots showing the no-training flag, runtime logs demonstrating that model-improvement pipelines were not fed tenant X's data (redacted where necessary), and the SOC 2 summary. For procurement we can provide an unredacted bundle under an NDA — please confirm recipient email for the evidence upload (we will use an encrypted transfer link).

Attachments included (in redwood-evidence-handoff.zip):
- SOC2_TypeII_Summary_2026.pdf (executive summary)
- Subprocessor_Inventory_20260618.csv
- NoTraining_Runtime_technote.txt (how the flag is enforced, sample logs)
- Pentest_ExecSummary_2026.pdf

Action items:
1) Mike — confirm the procurement/legal recipients for the evidence bundle and whether Stratus requires immediate deletion at POC end or 30/60/90 day window.
2) Anna — will review the DPA addendum language and propose any redlines. I'll share a draft by end of day and attach the evidence bundle via an encrypted link.

If helpful, Neha can join a short 30-minute technical call to walk your security team through the runtime isolation and logging model.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Trust & Safety — Redwood Inference
